IBoundaryRepresentation

## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Boundary representation (BREP) interfaces
//
// The exact, resolution-independent solid encoding: a shell of vertices,
// undirected edges, and faces, where each face bounds itself with loops of
// oriented EDGE-USES (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boundary_representation).
// One undirected edge owns one curve; the two adjacent faces cite that edge
// with opposite orientations. This is deliberately NOT the half-edge encoding:
// `HalfEdgeMesh` (topology.types.plato) duplicates every edge into two
// directed sides and is the DISCRETE tessellation IR — BREP shells tessellate
// INTO it (or into TriangleMesh3D), never the other way. Half-edge
// `BoundaryLoop` is a hole walk in a mesh and is not reused here; the BREP
// face loop is `BrepLoop` (brep.types.plato).
//
// Closedness is a proof, not a flag: no `ClosedShell` marker is stamped on
// `Brep3D`, because an unvalidated marker is a stale claim waiting to happen.
// A shell is shown closed by `IsWatertight` / `Validate` (brep.library.plato);
// a validated subtype (`ClosedBrep3D` produced only by a proving constructor)
// is the planned future encoding of that proof.

// The capability marker for boundary-representation solids: an exact shell of
// vertices, curve-carrying undirected edges, and surface-carrying faces bounded
// by oriented edge-uses. Implementations stay resolution-independent until
// explicitly tessellated.
interface IBoundaryRepresentation
    inherits ISolid
{ }
```
